notes:
PASS on the fake backend only: python3 -m mhs.driver check MHS/drivers/robots/pocketxjl__humanoid-control --backend fake exited 0; evidence contract_checked, never an MHS-Device level. Model-authored and unreviewed: driver.lock.json authored_by is the model deepseek-v4.1-flash:1017 (run ros-wave-c-005) and reviewed_by stays null. No human reviewed or tested this package, no hardware was attached, and no hardware, ROS, Gazebo or upstream-simulator run is claimed.

DEVIATION FROM THE CARD: the card is family-config with family ros and helper RosDriver, but this repository is a MuJoCo simulation: mujoco_sim/script/humanoid_sim.py imports mujoco, sets data.ctrl from joint targets and calls mj_step (humanoid_sim.py:110-112), and the card's only model is the MJCF humanoid-legged-description/mjcf/humanoid_legged.xml:1 (role sim-env; candidate classes cap.world.step/reset/seed.v1; entry_symbols empty). A RosDriver is a topic/service/action transport; it cannot own a step or reset of this continuously running C++ controller, and the clone exposes no stop service or action (only topics, plus the unacknowledged pauseFlag Bool). The primary interface for the card's model is the MuJoCo world step, so this package is a configuration-only MujocoDriver over the MJCF. The switch is recorded here for a card override; task.json was not edited.

WHAT IT SERVES: cap.world.step.v1 {ticks, action:{ctrl:[12]}} and cap.world.reset.v1. The bridge derives per-actuator ctrl bounds from the model's actuator_ctrlrange on humanoid_legged.xml:156-167, writes data.ctrl, calls mj_step ticks times, and returns observation {time, qpos, qvel}, tick and state_hash. reset calls mj_resetData + mj_forward. State: time_ms, qpos, qvel, ctrl, tick, timestep_ms, seed. The model has a free base and 12 leg hinges (19 qpos, 18 qvel); ctrl has 12 motor channels. No seed class is served: this model has no random number generator, and the seed field is metadata.

NOT COVERED: the OCS2 NMPC/WBC controller, the linear Kalman state estimator, the ROS 1 nodes/topics, the gait command publisher, the MuJoCo viewer/camera/rendering, and the arm/head/waist meshes (they are visual geoms with no joints or actuators in this MJCF). The package serves the low-level plant world, not the upstream walking-controller environment. The upstream sim also computes targetTorque + Kp*(targetPos - qpos) + Kd*(targetVel - qvel) before mj_step (humanoid_sim.py:110); this driver writes ctrl directly, so a deployment must supply that composite torque or run the upstream controller separately. The upstream manual start pose (base z 1.225 and init_joint_pos, humanoid_sim.py:14-16,50-53) is not reproduced by mj_resetData, and the model has no keyframe. Only the 12 leg motors are controllable; arms/head/waist are not actuated.

FAKE/FIDELITY: MuJoCo is not installed where the gate ran and the card's install block has no commands, so backends['fake'] is this package's analytic stand-in mujoco module (fake.py). It parses the same MJCF for actuator count/ranges and joint dimensions and integrates a placeholder first-order motion, not MuJoCo physics. The fake backend publishes F0 with engine 'analytic:stand-in mujoco module (no physics)'; the F1 contract 'mujoco:humanoid_legged_description' is declared for the implicit live sim backend that imports the official mujoco module and was not run. The model's timestep is 0.001 s (humanoid_legged.xml:4); the published timestep_ms is 1.0 in both contracts. No trajectory was compared with the real engine or the upstream simulator.

SAFETY: simulated world at R0, no hardware backend and no route to a physical humanoid. The runtime software latch refuses step and reset after an e-stop until safety reset; the bridge holds a lock around mutations. There is no native stop to claim; SAFE-045 applies to hardware/hybrid R2+, which this package is not. No hardware run or hardware backend exists. The model's joint position ranges (humanoid_legged.xml:85-144) are MuJoCo limits, not package Limits; the control envelope is the actuator ctrlrange derivation.

GATE: all required gates pass. G6.NOT_RECORDED and G7.UPSTREAM_BACKEND are the expected simulator-family warnings because the fake is a stand-in mujoco module, and G8.NO_UNIT x3 are the expected ticks/action.ctrl[*]/seed unit warnings. There was no G4.REF_VALUE or G4.REF_BINARY warning. test_driver.py keeps the check_driver call and adds six model-specific cases; G9 passed. No catalogue_requests: only cap.world.step.v1 and cap.world.reset.v1 are used. The clone was read only and was not modified; no file outside the package was written. check-report.json is the gate's own report.

MODEL REVIEW (claude-opus-5-5, a model and not a human, 2026-11-05; reviewed_by stays null): Checked the MujocoDriver deviation, all 14 facts, the derived ctrlrange envelope and the stand-in mujoco module against humanoid_legged.xml, humanoid_sim.py, mujoco_base.py, humanoidController.cpp and CheatControllerNode.cpp at the pin. The deviation is right (the card's only model is the MJCF and the repository's own runtime steps it with mj_step; the ROS topics carry the controller loop, and pauseFlag is an unacknowledged Bool), the twelve ctrlranges and joint ranges match the MJCF lines, and the lockstep software latch does stop this simulation from advancing. One fact cited CheatControllerNode.cpp:25-48 for a controller.update call that is on line 65; the reviewer changed the ref to 25-69 in driver.py and facts.md and regenerated reference.json, REFERENCE.md and check-report.json. The gate and collect.py --strict pass with the expected MuJoCo-family warnings (G6.NOT_RECORDED, G7.UPSTREAM_BACKEND, G8.NO_UNIT) and the digest unchanged. For the human reviewer: The package serves the bare plant: raw ctrl torques on twelve leg motors with no OCS2/WBC controller, so the humanoid falls unless a caller supplies the controller's composite torque; reset restores the MJCF defaults, not the upstream start pose. No hardware path exists.
